English.Char_Desc_45: Live AI usage limits on the Windows desktop
English.Char_Desc_80: Windows 11 widget: live Claude, Codex, Copilot, Antigravity, Grok, Cursor limits
English.Char_Desc_250: A tiny native Windows 11 floating overlay that shows your AI usage limits on the desktop: Claude, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Google Antigravity, xAI Grok and Cursor. It reads nothing before you allow it, needs no API key, and sends no telemetry.
English.Char_Desc_450: AI Limits is a tiny native Windows 11 floating overlay that shows how much of each AI subscription window you have used and when it resets: Claude, Codex, Copilot, Antigravity, Grok and Cursor. It reads the sign-ins your tools already keep, read-only and only once you allow each one; Cursor gets a sign-in of its own in the browser. No API key, no account, no telemetry. Free and open source, GPL-3.0.
English.Char_Desc_2000:
AI Limits reads the sign-ins of the AI tools already on your computer - Claude Code, Codex CLI, the GitHub CLI, the Antigravity CLI (agy), the Grok CLI - once you allow each one, and shows the usage limits behind them, live, on the desktop: how much of each window is used and when it resets. Claude's 5-hour and weekly windows, plus the Fable, Opus and Sonnet weeks on plans that have them. Codex's session and weekly windows. Copilot's premium requests, chat and completions. Antigravity's shared model pools. Grok's weekly SuperGrok limit. Cursor's included usage, through a sign-in of the app's own in the browser.
Nothing of another tool is read before you allow it: the first start asks, naming every file and where each token goes. Sign-ins are read read-only and never refreshed, so your tools stay signed in. Antigravity's row needs the Antigravity CLI (agy) and reads "token expired" until agy is run again; the app warns first that Google has suspended some accounts for using that sign-in outside Antigravity. Each token goes only to the provider that issued it. No telemetry, no server of ours.
Rows and models chooses the rows the widget and the tooltip show, extra rows where a provider meters a part on its own, and an optional model label. Closed, the widget folds into a tray icon with two rings, or a mini panel beside the tray showing a percentage, the time to the reset, or both. A source that is down leaves its last reading grey, with its age. It never invents a number.
Measured on the audited release build: about 0.005% of one CPU core at idle, no GPU time at all (the interface is drawn on the CPU), and around 37 MB of memory. A 3 MB executable, statically linked, no runtime to install, no admin rights needed.
Three detail levels, several layouts, nine palettes; opacity, brightness and saturation are adjustable, and the context menu shows each look before you click it. Free and open source under GPL-3.0; the source is on GitHub.
